stem_text: A mass of 1 kg is kept on an inclined plane with 30^(∘) inclination with respect to horizontal plane and it is at rest initially. Then the whole assembly is moved up with constant velocity of 4m/s . The work done by the frictional force in time 2 s is ____ J. (Take 𝑔=10m/s^(2) )

candidate_solve.derivation: Block rests on incline at theta = 30 deg. Tangential gravity balance gives static friction f_s = mg sin(30 deg) = 1 * 10 * 0.5 = 5 N directed up the incline. The incline assembly translates vertically upward at constant v = 4 m/s for t = 2 s, so vertical displacement s_y = 4 * 2 = 8 m. Since acceleration a = 0, dynamic equilibrium holds and f_s remains 5 N up the incline. Incline angle is 30 deg to horizontal, so friction vector angle to vertical is 60 deg (or angle to horizontal is 30 deg). Vertical component of static friction f_s,y = f_s * sin(30 deg) = 5 * 0.5 = 2.5 N. Work done by friction W = f_s,y * s_y = 2.5 N * 8 m = 20 J.
candidate_solve.limiting_cases: If theta = 0 deg, f_s = 0 => W = 0 J. If theta -> 90 deg, normal force -> 0 (block falls). For theta = 30 deg, W = 20 J.

sl2.crux: Recognizing that static friction can perform non-zero work in an inertial frame when the contact boundary translates, and projecting friction onto the displacement vector.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Equilibrium static friction and definition of work W = F . s.

representation_translation.evidence: Resolving inclined vector into vertical motion coordinate.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Equilibrium force -> vertical component -> displacement dot product.

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Overcoming the pervasive misconception that static friction never does work.

wrong_route_hypotheses.route: Claiming W = 0 because static friction does no work relative to the surface
Using full magnitude without projecting W = f_s * s = 5 * 8 = 40 J
Projecting using cos(30) instead of sin(30): W = 5 * cos(30) * 8 = 34.6 J
